title: How many numbers lie between these pairs of squares?
description: The video counts the numbers between the squares of sixteen and seventeen, and between the squares of ninety nine and one hundred. It then subtracts the squares to check each count.
teaching_notes: One idea: between the squares of n and n plus one there are two times n numbers. Watch for students who subtract the squares and forget to take away one for the end number.

video_script.why: The child applies the method of the solved example, subtract the squares and leave out the end number, in the form two times n.
video_script.substitution: Use two times the smaller number to count the numbers between the squares of two numbers next to each other.
video_script.anchor: the two pairs of numbers, sixteen and seventeen, and ninety nine and one hundred, each with a square sign and an empty answer box
video_script.payoff_line: There are thirty two numbers in the first case and one hundred ninety eight in the second

final_answer.spoken: thirty two numbers, and one hundred ninety eight numbers

never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: between n² and (n + 1)² there are 2n numbers
video_script.design: One idea: two times the smaller number counts the numbers between two squares next to each other. The two pairs stay in the anchor band and the counts fill in beside them.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Take the squares of sixteen and seventeen.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Then take the squares of ninety nine and one hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many numbers lie between the two squares, in each case?

beats.on_screen: 3² = 9 and 4² = 16 at the ends of a number line; 16 − 9 = 7, then 7 − 1 = 6; 6 = 2 × 3

marks.ends: 9 and 16 appear at the two ends of a number line

narration: <bookmark mark='ends'/>Use the same method as for twenty five and thirty six. Take three squared and four squared, which are nine and sixteen.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>Sixteen minus nine is seven, and one less is six.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Six is two times three, and three is the smaller of the two numbers.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many numbers lie between the two squares in each pair

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to count the numbers between the two squares in each pair.

beats.on_screen: between n² and (n + 1)² there are 2n numbers

marks.rule: the line between n² and (n + 1)² there are 2n numbers is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, between the squares of n and n plus one there are two times n numbers. Here n is the smaller number of the pair.
<bookmark mark='n'/>Step two, in the first pair the smaller number is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Two times sixteen is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='n'/>Step three, in the second pair the smaller number is ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Two times ninety nine is one hundred ninety eight.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step four, put the answers back in the question. Two hundred eighty nine minus two hundred fifty six, less one, is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Ten thousand minus nine thousand eight hundred one, less one, is one hundred ninety eight.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>There are thirty two numbers in the first case and one hundred ninety eight in the second.
